prior_main_text: A man pauses to pray before the day begins. Continue with an invitation to bring our concerns to the Father.
A vision for learning at home
Act. Practice one truth in prayer, relationships, worship, or service.

Before reading, name the help you hope to receive. Afterward, write one thing the passage teaches about Jesus Christ and one question you would like to keep studying. Let an unanswered question remain part of tomorrow’s prayer.
Begin with the official lesson, then use scholarly context without letting commentary replace scripture.
Begin with the scriptures, notice what they reveal about Jesus Christ, and let one truth shape the way you live this week.
Carry Learning into a Helpful Act
Carry a passage or an honest question into Ask. Read the supporting sources and return to the scripture as you consider the response.
Choose a phrase that draws your attention. Follow a footnote or the lesson’s cross-reference. Compare the passages carefully, and leave room for a question you cannot yet answer.
Choose a topic-based video, read its study context, and discuss one idea before moving on. The Watch library keeps the media and its sources together.
Choose one verse, one question, and one small activity. Invite each person to share a thought or listen quietly.
Choose the setting that fits your life today. Every path returns to scripture and Jesus Christ.
Come, Follow Me—For Home and Church: Old Testament 2026

Consider how the passage could shape an ordinary moment today: your patience, an apology, a generous act, or time with someone who needs care. Choose one response you can carry out, then return to your notes later and reflect on what you learned.
Explore Doctrine and Covenants 6:32–37, related scripture, historical setting, and practical ways to keep Christ in your thoughts.
Explore the April 2026 General Conference study collection. Follow a message that relates to the principle you are studying.
Explore the Look Unto Me study →
Explore the artwork and its study connections. Describe what you notice, then read the connected scripture in its own setting.
Explore ways to share faith with care and respect. Consider whom you could listen to, encourage, or help this week.
Find a study for real life
Find help with questions about prayer, faith, family, grief, or something you noticed in your reading.
Follow the journeys and historical questions. Consider courage and community while learning the circumstances of the people involved.
For official guidance on context, questions, recording impressions, and learning together, see

Ideas for individuals, families, and Church classes
Ideas to Improve Learning at Home and at Church
Ideas to Improve Learning at Home and at Church

Invite each person to share one observation without pressure to give the same answer. Choose a specific act of kindness, a prayer, or a conversation to follow your study. Return later and record what you noticed.
Let a passage stay with you
Let one question open a deeper journey
Look for Christ. Notice what the Lord does, promises, teaches, or asks.
Make room to watch and ponder
Meet the people of the Restoration through their stories and surviving records. Read what happened, then consider what you want to learn from their lives.
Official Come, Follow Me materials and guidance
One steadies the gate while the other tightens its hinge. Their shared effort offers a simple place to begin when scripture study leads to an act of service.
Open any month and move directly to its official weekly lesson. The current month and lesson are highlighted automatically.
Open the official manual and choose the lesson for your week.
Read “Turn to God before the day begins” in Jesus Christ →
Pause with this short introduction from the Church’s teaching-video collection. After watching, consider one change that could help your study draw you closer to Jesus Christ.
Read slowly, mark repeated ideas, write an honest question, and act on one impression.
Read the lesson introduction. Write one question you are carrying.
Read the opening portion. Mark repeated names, promises, warnings, and invitations.

Read the verses around your chosen passage. Identify who is speaking, who is listening, and what question or situation the passage addresses. Write down what the text says before deciding what it means for you.

Return to a phrase that drew your attention. Read the surrounding verses and record the thought or invitation you want to remember. If studying with others, invite each person to share or simply listen; a quiet response is welcome too.

See the year’s scripture journey in context
Seven days of scripture and discipleship
Share one truth about Christ, record one impression, and choose one action.
Start with the official Church lesson. These illustrated links lead to the manual and learning resources, so you can choose the help you need.

Study together. Choose one verse and make room for every person to share.
The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints · Videos for Individuals and Families
The announced 2027 Come, Follow Me curriculum is the New Testament. Return here when the new year begins to continue your study.
The schedule helps pace study, but conversion is the purpose. Return to the Lord, the scriptures, sincere questions, and faithful action.
There is no need to hurry past a verse that deserves your attention. Choose one of these invitations, bring your scriptures, and give yourself a quiet moment to respond.
Try this during any week of study, on your own or with someone else. Bring your scriptures and a notebook, and begin with the official lesson.
Turn to God before the day begins
Use the official lesson. Follow one question or cross-reference that deepens understanding.
Use the rest of focusChrist alongside your weekly reading. Each pathway offers a different way to study, reflect, and put learning into practice.
Use the whole pattern or choose one step. The purpose is not to finish a checklist. It is to hear the Lord and follow Him.
Watch the 2-minute, 44-second introduction, then return to one passage and the reflection you want to carry into your day.
What do these chapters reveal about His character and work?
What helps me look to Christ?
What will I carry into today?
What will you do because of what you learned?
Which promise, warning, or invitation points you toward Him?

A closed scripture book and seven blank cards suggest making room for scripture throughout a week. The waiting cards invite a simple question: when will you pause to read and ponder this week?

Read with the landscape in mind
Terraces, olive trees, and limestone hills evoke the geography of scripture study. This is an illustrative landscape, not a verified biblical location or a reconstruction of a particular event.
